super_tldr: A local-first, privacy-respecting Outlook email and calendar security tool. Scan your messages and events for stale or sensitive items, preview security actions, and apply archiving, sensitivity labels, read-state changes, and calendar cleanup. No server, no sync, no cloud copy of your data.
human_purpose: Help Mark secure his Outlook emails and calendar by finding old messages, bulk-archiving them into a secured folder, applying sensitivity labels (Private), marking messages as read, setting importance levels, removing follow-up flags, applying categories, and cleaning up stale calendar events by setting sensitivity, canceling old meetings, or updating show-as status. All actions are previewed before applying.
concept_entrances: what this app does and does not do
how to connect your Outlook account
how security scan suggestions are generated
how to preview before applying security actions
how to archive emails to a secured folder
how to apply sensitivity labels to emails
how to mark messages as read in bulk
how to secure calendar events and cancel old meetings
authority: the human authorizes every security action
no action is taken without explicit preview-and-confirm
access tokens stay in browser memory only
no data is sent anywhere except Microsoft Graph
Creation records tool lineage only, never your emails or calendar data
privacy: OAuth tokens are held in browser memory and session storage only
no telemetry, analytics, or remote logging
no server component stores or proxies your data
disconnecting clears all cached tokens and action log
all scanning and security actions run locally in your browser
permissions_rationale: Mail.ReadWrite is needed to list, read, move (archive), and update message properties (sensitivity, isRead, importance, categories, flag)
Calendars.ReadWrite is needed to list and update calendar events (sensitivity, showAs, cancellation)

data_lifecycle.ingress: Microsoft Graph API via OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE
data_lifecycle.storage: In-memory only; access tokens cleared on disconnect or tab close
data_lifecycle.egress: None — no data leaves the browser except API responses from Microsoft Graph
data_lifecycle.retention: Tokens and preferences expire when the browser tab closes or the user disconnects
data_lifecycle.disposal: Disconnect button purges all session state immediately

risks: Canceling calendar meetings sends cancellation notices to attendees — only applies to meetings you organized
Sensitivity labels require Exchange/Office 365 to have them configured; the app falls back gracefully if not available
Large batch operations may hit Graph API throttling limits; the app retries with exponential backoff
Archived messages moved to the Secure Archive folder remain in your mailbox, not permanently deleted
Only your own mailbox and calendar are accessed; no other user's data is touched

email: archive — move messages to a secured Secure Archive folder
sensitivity — set message sensitivity (normal, personal, private, confidential)
importance — set importance level (low, normal, high)
flag — clear or set follow-up flag
calendar: cancel — cancel meetings you organized (sends notice to attendees)
